entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *barbarous*: condemns as a whole civilisation would: this is beneath what people owe each other.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *light-hearted*: the hyphenated spelling, equally common and equally warm.
examples: he light-heartedly overlooks some of the basic facts of life

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flattery with coaxing added - the praise is a lever being worked.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Striking enough to arrest attention.
examples: quite stunning with large dark eyes and a beautiful high-bosomed figure
stunning photographs of Canada's wilderness areas

entries.definition: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Abandoned as well as ruined - nobody is coming back for it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Archaic on its own; nearly always heard in the longer form.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The gentlest euphemism of all, and the one most used with children.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Sharpness of perception; it praises the seeing rather than the knowing.
examples: much too perspicacious to be taken in by such a spurious argument

entries.definition: marked by skill in achieving a desired end especially with cunning or craft
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Skill first, deceit second - it can admire the craft even while it disapproves.

entries.definition: quietly and steadily persevering especially in detail or exactness
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same steadiness against resistance; it presumes there was reason to stop.
examples: with persevering (or patient) industry she revived the failing business

entries.definition: having or fostering a warm or friendly and informal atmosphere
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Of an atmosphere rather than a person - and it turns critical the moment it takes an object: cozy with the regulators.
examples: the small room was cozy and intimate

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most emphatic and the least used of the three.

entries.definition: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Caution that was earned rather than a fault - what experience leaves behind.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Order was lost rather than never present - the pieces are all still there.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *voracious*: appetite at full stretch - the eating is hard to satisfy.

entries.definition: being of delicate or slender build
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The polite compliment - thin in a way people want to be.
examples: a slim girl with straight blonde hair
She stayed slim into her seventies.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word - direct, and sometimes faintly accusing depending on who says it.
examples: many fond hopes are pinned on rich uncles

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Older and quieter than *happy*, and it points at a reason.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Casual and brief, with no attitude attached.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Borrows the language of madness; the anger is presented as beyond reason.
examples: could not control the maddened crowd

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The rarer verb beside the common noun; the same quiet correction.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A back-formation from uncouth, and almost always a joke; nobody is seriously called couth.

entries.definition: without pity; in a merciless manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *pitiless*: said as easily of weather and landscape as of people, and just as final.

entries.definition: having or marked by unusual and impressive intelligence
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Affectionate and slightly teasing admiration.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *wholehearted*: the common form, and the one that still gets used in earnest.
examples: he adopted wholeheartedly some of the policies that he had previously criticized

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *distrustful*: states the position without explaining it - the trust is simply absent.

entries.definition: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word, and the one that carries a second, moral life (*a dirty trick*).

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *untidy*: the plain word, and a small complaint - it expects the state to be temporary.

entries.definition: in a curious and questioning manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The adverb of *questioning*: the plainest form: the questions are being asked, and nothing is implied about why.
examples: they turned their heads questioningly, as if awaiting further instructions

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grave and literary - deaths in numbers, or deaths that should not have happened.
examples: The children perished in the fire

entries.definition: suspicious or unduly suspicious or fearful of being displaced by a rival
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fear of being displaced. The older sense - jealous of one's honour - was closer to vigilance.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Headline language: loud, public and short, with no pretence of fairness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Complaint dressed as distress - dismisses the cause as trivial.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gloss is *embarrassingly stingy* - the shame is the point, and it is public.
examples: He's too cheap to tip properly.
Don't be cheap - buy the good coffee.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday version, mild enough to say to someone's face.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: It certifies good faith rather than admiring it.

entries.definition: not wise in the ways of the world
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Can be reproach or admiration, depending entirely on what the world is thought to be worth.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The everyday word, and the one that emphasises secrecy over skill.

entries.definition: ill-mannered and coarse and contemptible in behavior or appearance
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Denies the person their own century; the insult is evolutionary.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The fourth humour. Anger arrives fast and is presented as constitutional.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The legal word: it implies a crime has been committed, not merely a lie told.
examples: a fraudulent scheme to escape paying taxes

entries.definition: having or showing feelings of unwarranted importance out of overbearing pride
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns self-importance as unearned - the confidence is real, the entitlement is not.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the position without explaining it - the trust is simply absent.
examples: my experience … in other fields of law has made me distrustful of rules of thumb generally

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *dogged*: the same refusal to yield, entirely admired - dogged is what stubborn is called when it wins.

entries.definition: having or showing a kindly or tender nature
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Kindness expressed as restraint - the force that was available was not used.
examples: the gentle touch of her hand

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *bounteous*: biblical in flavour, and hard to use now without irony.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disorder that suggests something happened - the state was not chosen.

entries.definition: deceptive or fraudulent; disposed to cheat or defraud or deceive
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Judges the breach of a code rather than the lie itself; what is lost is standing, not just truth.
